name: gui_build_D
description: GB-1 target D (shadows), from File > New Project > Blank with Studio's GUI only, on the Graph tab. As gui_build_B: the palette adds a render.material_pass of deferred_geometry_v1, Add Object > Cube and Add Object > Floor (a board under the box) give it something to draw, and Add fullscreen pass adds the lighting pass. Its Frame data's Uses scene lights is ticked first, so the frame has a lighting pass of its own; Features: shadow_directional picked in the catalog, Add, Apply -- RS-10 takes it for the deferred pipeline (no material or fullscreen consumer needed), and the frame plan draws shadow_map first. Back on the Graph tab, the lighting pass's New... > Deferred lighting > Create (UX-5b) writes the template with the shadow parts: shadow_map is one of its inputs, read through a render.target_ref the same edit adds, and the feature defines PELICAN_FEATURE_SHADOW for it. The lighting pass's colour dragged onto present's + input, the viewport shows the lit box and its shadow on the floor: a floor point on the box's left side is not the colour of the point opposite it on the right. UX-12c: the material pass's Materials drawn names what the engine says it drew in a published frame (the Cube's and the Floor's primitive default materials, not the built-in transparent one), and Add binding's name is picked from the engine's list (the row, told nothing to read, sends nothing and is removed). Not built by hand: the shadow depth pass itself is the feature's (shadow_directional), not a render.shadow_depth from the palette. Typed: the project folder and the name gb_d in New Project, and material_pass in the palette's filter.
